official.status_note: SUSS publishes two annual application periods: 'Scholarship application period: January Semester: 1 August to 15 September; July Semester: 1 February to 15 March'. As at 10 October 2026 the January Semester window had closed and the July Semester window opens on 1 February.
official.tuition_coverage_note: SUSS's terms state: 'The value of the scholarship covers 100% of course fee (inclusive of government subsidy) for recipient's remaining candidature of study. It includes course materials, examination fee and other compulsory fees, as well as miscellaneous fees. There is no bond attached to the scholarship.'

verification.notes: suss.edu.sg returned HTTP 403 to every direct fetch (multiple webfetch and PowerShell attempts), so the benefit wording, application windows and outcome dates were taken from the official domain's own indexed text of the scholarship page and of the official SUSS Scholarship (For Part-time Undergraduates) terms-and-conditions PDF. Confidence is therefore low. No monetary figure is published by SUSS. Note that the catalogue's 'fully funded' label overstates this award: SUSS covers course fees, materials, examination and compulsory fees and miscellaneous fees, but publishes no living cost component, so fully_funded is recorded as false.

applicant_utility.summary: The award is a fee-cover award, not a living award: it pays 100% of the course fee including the government subsidy for your remaining candidature, plus course materials, examination and other compulsory fees and miscellaneous fees, but it puts nothing in your pocket while you study part-time. Law students are excluded outright, and new students have to be admitted first, so you cannot apply for the scholarship and admission simultaneously. Watch the two intakes, because the January Semester window closes on 15 September and the July Semester one on 15 March, with outcomes only by end November and end June respectively.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Working Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents with a strong prior academic record and a substantial co-curricular and community-service history entering a SUSS part-time degree.
application_readiness_checklist: If you are a new student, submit the SUSS admission e-application first and wait for acceptance before the scholarship form.
Diarise both intakes: 1 August to 15 September for the January Semester, and 1 February to 15 March for the July Semester.
Check you are not heading into a Law programme, which the scholarship does not cover.
Read the SUSS e-guide before starting the online application, as SUSS directs applicants to it.
Submit by the closing date rather than trailing the window, since applications are processed against the stipulated date.
common_rejection_risks: Applying before admission is confirmed, which is a stated precondition for new students.
Enrolling in a Law programme, which is excluded from the scholarship.
Missing the 15 September or 15 March closing date.
Falling outside the Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident categories.
Expecting an appeal; SUSS states no reasons are given for non-selection and no appeals are entertained.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs while studying part-time, transport, and anything outside the course fee, course materials, examination fee, other compulsory fees and miscellaneous fees are not covered.
document_audit: No document checklist is published on the page; the stated requirement is an online application by the closing date, so keep transcripts and CCA records ready in case a later stage asks for them.
New students must complete the admission e-application separately first, so two submissions are needed in sequence.
The award is tied to your remaining candidature, so transferring or extending your programme changes what is covered.
Check the same SUSS page for the separate donor-funded awards and sponsorships for part-time undergraduates, which have their own applications.
alerts: The award covers your remaining candidature only, so a student who applies late into the programme gets fewer years of cover than one who applies at entry.
SUSS's decision is final and binding, with no reasons given and no appeals entertained.
Outcome notifications arrive by email, by end November for the January Semester and end June for the July Semester, so monitor the inbox the application was submitted from.

The same SUSS page lists donor-funded awards such as the Kewalram Chanrai Group Scholarship, the Hong Leong Foundation Scholarship, the ST Engineering - SUSS Scholarship and the UOB Future Resilience Scholarship; this record covers only the SUSS Scholarship.
Because the page blocked automated verification, re-check the current window dates on the SUSS site before relying on them.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission e-application for new students, then the online scholarship application by the closing date, then an email outcome from the Student Awards Committee.
